title: An Optimistic Gradient Tracking Method for Distributed Minimax Optimization: the key optimality-gap contraction lemma (Lemma 4)
author: Yan Huang, Jinming Xu, Jiming Chen, and Karl Henrik Johansson
work: An Optimistic Gradient Tracking Method for Distributed Minimax Optimization
difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the paper's own key lemma on the contraction of the optimality gap (the author announces it in exactly those words at source0.tex line 597) and it is carried by the longest proof block of the paper, 121 lines, longer than the 53-line proof of Theorem 1. Even with the paper's three supporting lemmas, its three assumptions and its update equations supplied as context, the proof is not a formal consequence of anything already proved: it has to build a one-step descent inequality for the optimality gap out of the averaged update rule (11), split the inner-product term with the strong-convexity-strong-concavity inequality and the smoothness inequality, recombine the pieces through the elementary identity a^2-2ab=(a-b)^2-b^2 into the numbered identity (30), bound the two remaining auxiliary terms, then invoke the consensus bound (25), the tracking bound (27) and Lemma 1's gap bound (24), tune the stepsize to the counted condition (28) so that the last four coefficients become non-positive, and finally complete the contraction with the two norm comparisons of its closing sentence. That is well beyond an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, where the convergence of first-order methods is examined for textbook gradient descent with a fixed stepsize and a standard Lyapunov function; but the devices used are the standard ones of the distributed-optimization literature (Young's inequality, smoothness, strong convexity, a Lyapunov/descent assembly), so the unit is recorded as H2 rather than H3.
